description.en: Stories of the Prophets drawn from the Quran, reliable tafsir, and Ibn Kathir’s Qisas al-Anbiya.
description.ar: قصص الأنبياء مستمدة من القرآن والتفاسير الموثوقة وقصص الأنبياء لابن كثير.

description.en: The life and noble character of Prophet Muhammad ﷺ.
description.ar: حياة النبي محمد ﷺ وشمائله الكريمة.

description.en: Companions of the Prophet ﷺ, including twelve key figures.
description.ar: صحابة النبي ﷺ، ومنهم اثنا عشر علماً من أعلامهم.

description.en: Short authentic accounts of the Tabi'un, successors, and other righteous predecessors.
description.ar: قبسات قصيرة موثقة من أخبار التابعين ومن بعدهم من السلف.

bio.en: The first human and prophet, taught the names and placed on earth as Allah’s vicegerent.
bio.ar: أول البشر والأنبياء، علّمه الله الأسماء وجعله خليفة في الأرض.

bio.en: A truthful prophet raised to a high station; called people back to Adam’s religion and taught justice and charity.
bio.ar: نبي صدّيق رفعه الله مكاناً عليّاً، دعا الناس إلى دين آبائه وعلّمهم العدل والصدقة.

bio.en: Called his people to worship Allah alone for centuries; those who believed were saved in the Ark from the Flood.
bio.ar: دعا قومه إلى عبادة الله وحده قروناً، ونجّى الله المؤمنين معه في السفينة من الطوفان.

bio.en: Sent to the powerful people of ‘Ad, who were arrogant builders; he called them to worship Allah alone.
bio.ar: أرسل إلى قوم عاد الأقوياء المتجبرين، فدعاهم إلى إفراد الله بالعبادة.

bio.en: Sent to Thamud after ‘Ad; called them to tawhid and warned them concerning the she-camel of Allah.
bio.ar: أرسل إلى ثمود بعد عاد، فدعاهم إلى التوحيد وحذّرهم في شأن ناقة الله.

bio.en: The Friend of Allah and father of the prophets, who broke the idols and called his people to pure tawhid.
bio.ar: خليل الله وأبو الأنبياء، كسّر الأصنام ودعا قومه إلى التوحيد الخالص.

bio.en: Son of Ibrahim, left with his mother Hajar in the barren valley of Makkah; linked to Zamzam and the Ka‘bah.
bio.ar: ابن إبراهيم، تُرك مع أمه هاجر في وادٍ غير ذي زرع بمكة، وارتبط باسم زمزم والبيت.

bio.en: Son of Ibrahim, granted after glad tidings; father of Yaqub and a prophet in the line of guidance.
bio.ar: ابن إبراهيم بُشّر به بعد الكبر، أبو يعقوب ونبي في سلسلة الهداية.

bio.en: Also called Israel; favored with prophethood, father of the twelve tribes including Yusuf.
bio.ar: يُدعى إسرائيل، آتاه الله النبوة، وأبو الأسباط الاثني عشر ومنهم يوسف.

bio.en: Nephew of Ibrahim, sent to the people of Sodom to forbid their open immorality and call them to Allah.
bio.ar: ابن أخي إبراهيم، أرسل إلى أهل سدوم لينهاهم عن الفواحش ويدعوهم إلى الله.

bio.en: Sent to Madyan; commanded worship of Allah alone and fair measure in trade, forbidding corruption.
bio.ar: أرسل إلى مدين، فأمرهم بعبادة الله وإيفاء الكيل والميزان ونهاهم عن الفساد.

bio.en: Son of Yaqub; thrown into a well, sold into Egypt, then raised by Allah through patience and trust to authority.
bio.ar: ابن يعقوب؛ أُلقي في الجبّ ثم بيع بمصر، فرفعه الله بالصبر والتوكل إلى الملك.

bio.en: Patient prophet stricken with severe trial in health and wealth; he turned to Allah and was restored.
bio.ar: نبيٌّ صابر ابتُلي في بدنه وماله، فأناب إلى الله فردّ عليه عافيته.

bio.en: Mentioned among the patient and righteous; Ibn Kathir places him among the prophets of firm resolve in obedience.
bio.ar: ذُكر مع الصابرين والصالحين، وعدّه ابن كثير فيمن ثبتوا على طاعة الله.

bio.en: Left his people in anger, was swallowed by the whale, then called upon Allah in the darkness and was rescued.
bio.ar: غادر قومه مغاضباً فالتقمه الحوت، فنادى الله في الظلمات فنجّاه.

bio.en: Sent to Pharaoh with clear signs; led the Children of Israel and received the Torah.
bio.ar: أرسل إلى فرعون بالآيات، وأخرج بني إسرائيل وأنزلت عليه التوراة.

bio.en: Brother of Musa and a prophet who supported him in calling Pharaoh and guiding the Israelites.
bio.ar: أخو موسى ونبيّ أيّده في دعوة فرعون وهداية بني إسرائيل.

bio.en: Known as Ezekiel; Ibn Kathir recounts him among the prophets after Musa who revived hope for the Israelites.
bio.ar: يُعرف بحزقيال؛ ذكره ابن كثير فيمن بعث بعد موسى لإحياء رجاء بني إسرائيل.

bio.en: Called his people away from idolatry; Ibn Kathir includes him among the prophets between Musa and the later messengers.
bio.ar: دعا قومه لترك الشرك، وعدّه ابن كثير في الأنبياء بين موسى ومن بعدهم.

bio.en: Samuel; appointed when the Israelites asked for a king after defeat, and guided them under Allah’s command.
bio.ar: شمويل؛ بُعث حين طلب بنو إسرائيل ملكاً بعد الهزيمة، فهداهم بأمر الله.

bio.en: Defeated Goliath, was given kingship and the Zabur, and judged with justice and beautiful remembrance of Allah.
bio.ar: هزم جالوت، وآتاه الله الملك والزبور، وقضى بالعدل وأكثر من ذكر الله.

bio.en: Inherited Dawud’s prophethood; taught the speech of birds and given dominion over jinn, men, and the wind.
bio.ar: ورث نبوة داود، وعُلّم منطق الطير وسُخّر له الجنّ والإنس والريح.

bio.en: Isaiah; advised the righteous king of his time and, according to Ibn Kathir, foretold later messengers.
bio.ar: شعيا؛ نصح ملك زمانه الصالح، وذكر ابن كثير أنه بشّر بمن يأتي من الرسل.

bio.en: Jeremiah; warned his people and lived through the trials of Jerusalem as related by Ibn Kathir.
bio.ar: أرميا؛ أنذر قومه وعاش محنة بيت المقدس كما روى ابن كثير.

bio.en: Preserved by Allah when cast among lions; a righteous figure of the Babylonian captivity in Ibn Kathir’s accounts.
bio.ar: نجّاه الله إذ أُلقي إلى الأسود؛ من صلحاء سبي بابل في روايات ابن كثير.

bio.en: Ezra; the Quranic account of one who passed by ruined dwellings and whom Allah caused to die a hundred years then raised.
bio.ar: عزير؛ صاحب قصة من مرّ على قرية خاوية فأماته الله مائة عام ثم بعثه.

bio.en: Elderly prophet who cared for Maryam and prayed for an heir; granted Yahya in his old age.
bio.ar: نبي طاعن في السن كفل مريم ودعا بالذرية، فوُهب يحيى على الكبر.

bio.en: Son of Zakariyah; given wisdom as a child, devout and merciful, holding fast to the Scripture.
bio.ar: ابن زكريا؛ أوتي الحكم صبيّاً، وكان تقيّاً رحيماً آخذاً بالكتاب بقوة.

bio.en: Son of Maryam, created by Allah’s word; a messenger supported with clear signs, not a son of God.
bio.ar: ابن مريم خلقه الله بكلمة منه، رسول مؤيّد بالآيات، وليس ابناً لله.

honorific.en: peace and blessings of Allah be upon him

bio.en: The Messenger of Allah, seal of the prophets.
bio.ar: رسول الله وخاتم النبيين.

honorific.en: may Allah be pleased with him

bio.en: The first caliph and the closest companion of the Prophet ﷺ.
bio.ar: أول الخلفاء الراشدين وأقرب أصحاب النبي ﷺ.

honorific.en: may Allah be pleased with him

bio.en: The second caliph, known as Al-Faruq.
bio.ar: ثاني الخلفاء الراشدين، الملقّب بالفاروق.

honorific.en: may Allah be pleased with him

bio.en: The third caliph, known as Dhun-Nurayn.
bio.ar: ثالث الخلفاء الراشدين، الملقّب بذي النورين.

honorific.en: may Allah be pleased with him

bio.en: The fourth caliph, cousin and son-in-law of the Prophet ﷺ.
bio.ar: رابع الخلفاء الراشدين، ابن عم النبي ﷺ وصهره.

honorific.en: may Allah be pleased with him

bio.en: Among the ten promised Paradise; known as Talhah the Generous.
bio.ar: من العشرة المبشرين بالجنة، يُعرف بطلحة الفيّاض.

honorific.en: may Allah be pleased with him

bio.en: Among the ten promised Paradise; hawari of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ.
bio.ar: من العشرة المبشرين بالجنة، حواري رسول الله ﷺ.

honorific.en: may Allah be pleased with him

bio.en: Among the ten promised Paradise; a trusted merchant and early emigrant.
bio.ar: من العشرة المبشرين بالجنة، تاجر أمين من السابقين المهاجرين.

honorific.en: may Allah be pleased with him

bio.en: Among the ten promised Paradise; the first to shoot an arrow in the path of Allah.
bio.ar: من العشرة المبشرين بالجنة، أول من رمى بسهم في سبيل الله.

honorific.en: may Allah be pleased with him

bio.en: Among the ten promised Paradise; an early convert from the Quraysh.
bio.ar: من العشرة المبشرين بالجنة، من السابقين إلى الإسلام من قريش.

honorific.en: may Allah be pleased with him

bio.en: Among the ten promised Paradise; Amin of this Ummah.
bio.ar: من العشرة المبشرين بالجنة، أمين هذه الأمة.

honorific.en: may Allah be pleased with her

bio.en: First wife of the Prophet ﷺ and the first to believe in his message.
bio.ar: زوج النبي ﷺ الأولى وأول من آمن برسالته.

honorific.en: may Allah be pleased with her

bio.en: Mother of the Believers and a foremost narrator of the Sunnah.
bio.ar: أم المؤمنين ومن أعلم رواة السنة.

honorific.en: may Allah have mercy on him

bio.en: A Tabi'i from Yemen, praised by the Prophet ﷺ for his devotion to his mother.
bio.ar: تابعي من اليمن، أثنى عليه النبي ﷺ لبرّه بوالدته.

content.en: When Ibrahim called his people to tawhid and exposed the helplessness of their idols, they answered with fury rather than reason. They gathered wood, kindled a tremendous fire, and prepared a catapult to cast him in. Their aim was to make an example of anyone who insulted their gods. Ibrahim’s certainty did not break. He sought help from none but Allah. As he was thrown, Allah commanded the fire: “Be coolness and safety upon Ibrahim.” The blaze that should have consumed him became a place of safety; he walked out while their plot failed. The Quran preserves this as a sign that creation obeys its Creator, and that those who trust Allah are not abandoned when people unite upon falsehood. Ibn Kathir places the fire after Ibrahim’s breaking of the idols and his public challenge, teaching that da‘wah may meet violence—yet Allah’s protection is nearer than the heat of any flame.
content.ar: لما دعا إبراهيم قومه إلى التوحيد وكسّر أصنامهم أوقدوا ناراً عظيمة وألقوه فيها. فقال الله: يا نار كوني برداً وسلاماً على إبراهيم. فلم تمسّه بسوء. نشأ إبراهيم بين من يعبدون الأصنام والكواكب والملوك. فحاجّهم أن المخلوق لا يكون إلهاً، ودعا أباه وقومه إلى الخالق الواحد. وكسّر الأصنام تاركاً كبيرها ليفضح باطلهم. فألقوه في نار عظيمة فجعلها الله برداً وسلاماً عليه. وواصل الدعوة، ثم أسكن هاجر وإسماعيل بمكة بأمر الله، ورفع مع إسماعيل قواعد البيت. فكانت حياته سيرة خليل آثر الحق على عادة قومه. وجمع ابن كثير هذه الابتلاءات لتظهر الشجاعة والعقل والتوكل.

stories.sourceCitation: Ibn Kathir, Stories of the Prophets (Qisas al-Anbiya); teaching paraphrase from the English edition

content.en: During the Hijrah, the Prophet ﷺ and Abu Bakr hid in the cave of Thawr. Abu Bakr said, "If one of them looks at his feet he will see us." The Prophet ﷺ replied, "What do you think of two, the third of whom is Allah?"
content.ar: في الهجرة اختبأ النبي ﷺ وأبو بكر في غار ثور. فقال أبو بكر: لو أن أحدهم نظر إلى قدميه لأبصرنا. فقال النبي ﷺ: «ما ظنك باثنين الله ثالثهما؟»

content.en: The Prophet ﷺ told Umar and Ali of a man from Yemen named Uways. He would have a white mark from illness, and he was deeply devoted to his mother. The Prophet ﷺ instructed them: if they met him, to ask him to seek forgiveness for them.
content.ar: أخبر النبي ﷺ عمر وعلياً برجل من اليمن اسمه أويس، به بياض من مرض، وكان بارّاً بوالدته. وأمرهما إن لقياه أن يستغفرا به.

content.en: Musa’s mother cast him into the river by revelation when Pharaoh was killing the sons of the Israelites. Pharaoh’s household picked him up; his sister watched, and he was returned to his mother’s breast under Allah’s plan. He grew in the palace, then fled after an accidental killing, finding shelter in Madyan and marriage after helping two women at the well. At the burning bush in the sacred valley, Allah spoke to him, gave him signs—the staff and the white hand—and sent him with Harun to Pharaoh. They demanded the release of the Children of Israel and called Pharaoh to Allah. Pharaoh’s sorcerers believed when Musa’s staff exposed their illusion; Pharaoh increased tyranny. Plagues followed as signs, yet he remained arrogant. Musa led the Israelites out by night. At the sea, Allah commanded him to strike with his staff; the sea parted and they crossed. Pharaoh’s army pursued and was drowned. At Sinai, Musa received the Tablets; in his absence some took the calf, and he returned in anger, then sought forgiveness for his people. Ibn Kathir’s long Musa chapter is a school of reliance, courage before tyrants, and the cost of breaking covenant after clear deliverance.
content.ar: نُجّي موسى رضيعاً من قتل فرعون للذكور، ورُبّي في القصر، ثم خرج بعد قتل خطأ. وعند النار كلّمه الله وأرسله مع هارون إلى فرعون. فأريا الآيات فتكبّر فرعون. وسار موسى ببني إسرائيل ليلاً. فلما حُصر بين الجند والبحر قال إن معي ربي سيهدين، فانفلق البحر وأُغرق فرعون. وأنزلت التوراة، وتتابعت هداية موسى في فتن قومه. وكتاب ابن كثير في موسى مدرسة شجاعة وتوكل وصدق أمام الطغاة.

content.en: Yunus was sent to a great city. When his people persisted in disbelief, he left before Allah’s command to depart, angry at their rejection. A storm rose at sea; lots were cast and he was thrown overboard, then swallowed by a great fish. In darkness upon darkness he called out: “There is no god but You; glory be to You; I have been among the wrongdoers.” Allah saved him. He was cast ashore weak, shaded by a plant, and restored. He returned to his people and found that they had believed after fearing punishment—so they were spared. Ibn Kathir teaches that even a prophet’s haste has consequences, yet sincere tasbih and tawbah open the door of mercy, and a nation’s repentance can lift approaching doom.
content.ar: غادر يونس قومه مغاضباً لتأخر إيمانهم. فهاج البحر وأُلقي ثم التقمه الحوت. فنادى في الظلمات: لا إله إلا أنت سبحانك إني كنت من الظالمين. فاستجاب الله ونجّاه. وأُلقي إلى الشاطئ وأنبت الله عليه شجرة، وآمن قومه من بعد. ويبرز ابن كثير دعاء الفرج المشهور.

timedCues.textAr: فاستجاب الله ونجّاه.

timedCues.textEn: He was cast ashore weak, shaded by a plant, and restored.
timedCues.textAr: وأُلقي إلى الشاطئ وأنبت الله عليه شجرة، وآمن قومه من بعد.

timedCues.textEn: He returned to his people and found that they had believed after fearing punishment—so they were spared.
timedCues.textAr: ويبرز ابن كثير دعاء الفرج المشهور.

timedCues.textEn: Ibn Kathir teaches that even a prophet’s haste has consequences, yet sincere tasbih and tawbah open the door of mercy, and a nation’s repentance can lift approaching doom.

content.en: Allah informed the angels that He would place successive generations of humankind on earth as caretakers. The angels asked about those who might shed blood, while they themselves glorified Allah. Allah answered that He knows what they do not know, then taught Adam the names of all things and asked the angels to name them. They admitted they knew only what He had taught them, and Adam spoke by Allah’s teaching, showing the honor given to humankind through knowledge. Allah commanded the angels to prostrate to Adam as a mark of respect. They all did so except Iblis, who refused out of arrogance, claiming he was better because he was created from fire while Adam was created from clay. For this pride Iblis was expelled from mercy and became an open enemy who vowed to mislead Adam’s offspring. Adam opened his eyes to a universe of obedience and rebellion, learning awe of Allah and the danger of envy. Adam was placed in Paradise. When he was alone, Allah created for him a partner, Eve (Hawwa), so that he might find tranquility. They were permitted every enjoyment except one tree. Satan whispered that the tree would make them angels or immortals, swearing he was a sincere adviser. They tasted it, felt shame, and covered themselves with leaves. Then they prayed: “Our Lord, we have wronged ourselves; if You do not forgive us we will be among the losers.” Allah accepted their repentance, for He is Oft-Forgiving, Most Merciful. They were sent down to earth for a time, with the promise that whoever follows Allah’s guidance will have no fear nor grief. Adam lived as the first prophet, calling his children to tawhid. Narrations related by Ibn Kathir describe clay taken for his creation, the covenant taken from Adam’s progeny (“Am I not your Lord?”), and later dialogue with Musa affirming that Adam’s slip had already been written in decree—yet repentance elevated him. His story teaches dignity through knowledge, the ruin of pride, and the nearness of Allah to those who turn back.

content.en: Idris followed the religion of Adam and Seth after people began to drift. Ibn Kathir relates that he called the people of Babylon to return to truth: justice between people, prayer, fasting on certain days, and giving a portion of wealth to the poor. Only a few listened, so he and those who believed moved on, continuing to teach fairness wherever they settled. The Quran names him among the truthful and the prophets, and states that Allah raised him to a high station. Commentators preserved wise sayings attributed to him about patience, honesty, and remembering death. Though his chapter is brief, Ibn Kathir places Idris as an early link in the chain of guidance—proof that whenever communities forget Allah, He sends callers who revive Adam’s path of tawhid and good character.

title.en: The Story of Nuh and the Ark

content.en: Long after Adam, Nuh’s people fell into idolatry. Ibn Kathir recounts that love for righteous men hardened into statues and then into worship of Wadd, Suwa‘, Yaghuth, Ya‘uq, and Nasr. Nuh was sent as a plain warner: worship Allah alone, fear the Day when deeds are judged, and leave the idols that cannot create or provide. He called them night and day, privately and in public. The chiefs mocked him as “only a man,” accused him of seeking status, and said the weak and poor who followed him proved his message was worthless. Nuh answered with patience that he asked no wage except from Allah, that he did not drive away the believers, and that he was only a sincere messenger. When their rejection grew extreme, Allah commanded him to build the Ark under watchful revelation. The people laughed as he built far from any sea. Then the oven overflowed and the Flood began. Believers boarded with pairs of creatures. Nuh called his son to embark; the son sought refuge on a mountain and was among the drowned. Nuh’s plea for his family was answered with the truth that kinship does not protect disbelief. Then the earth was told to swallow its water and the sky to withhold rain. The Ark came to rest, and the wrongdoers were destroyed. Ibn Kathir presents Nuh’s long da‘wah as the model of steadfast calling: sincerity without arrogance, mercy without compromise, and trust that victory belongs to Allah alone.
content.ar: دعا نوح قومه زمناً طويلاً إلى ترك الأصنام وعبادة الله وحده. فسخر منه الملأ وقالوا إنه في ضلال، فصبر وقال إنما هو رسول ناصح. وصنع السفينة بأمر الله. فلما جاء الطوفان ركب المؤمنون ومعهم من كل زوجين اثنين. وطلب ابنه جبلاً يعصمه فكان من المغرقين. ثم قيل للأرض أن تبلع ماءها وللسماء أن تقلع، واستوت السفينة وهلك الظالمون. وبقيت القصة آية لمن يعتبر. ويسوق ابن كثير ذلك من القرآن ليعلّم الثبات على دعوة التوحيد.

content.en: After the people of Nuh, the tribe of ‘Ad arose between Yemen and Oman. They were tall, strong builders of lofty structures, blessed with gardens and wealth, yet they joined idols with Allah and grew proud of their power. Hud, one of them, was sent with the same foundation every prophet taught: worship Allah alone, seek His forgiveness, and do not act as criminals on the earth. He reminded them of the favors they enjoyed and warned of a Day when none can help another. They listened but called him foolish or bewitched, demanding he bring the punishment if he was truthful. Hud declared his trust in Allah and dissociated from their shirk. Clouds they hoped would bring rain became a destructive wind by Allah’s command, raging for days and leveling what they trusted in. Hud and those who believed were saved. Ibn Kathir frames ‘Ad as a warning that strength, architecture, and abundance become a curse when they feed arrogance and drown out the call to tawhid.

title.en: The Story of Salih and the She-Camel

content.en: Thamud succeeded ‘Ad in power. They carved elegant homes in the rocky hills, yet fell into idolatry and oppression. Salih called them to worship Allah alone and to remember the fate of earlier nations. They demanded a miracle as proof. By Allah’s leave, a she-camel emerged as a clear sign, with rights to water on appointed days. Some believed, but many resented the camel for sharing their water and frightening their cattle. They plotted in secret, hamstrung her, and threatened Salih. He warned them of three days. They did not repent. After his warning, a crushing cry seized the wrongdoers in their dwellings, while Salih and the believers were delivered. Ibn Kathir stresses that when Allah’s sign is rejected after it arrives in plain view, excuses collapse. Craftsmanship and carved stone could not shield a people who mocked the messenger and harmed what Allah had made sacred.

content.en: Ibrahim grew up among people who worshipped idols, stars, and kings. From childhood his insight pushed him to question statues that neither speak nor benefit. He reasoned about the celestial bodies: a setting star, moon, or sun cannot be the Lord who never fails. He declared his face turned to the One who originated the heavens and the earth, free of partnership. He called his father Azar and his people to leave idols. When they left for a festival, he broke the idols, leaving the largest so they might ask it—if it could speak. Enraged, they kindled a great fire and cast him into it. Allah commanded: “O fire, be coolness and safety upon Ibrahim.” He emerged unharmed, then continued calling to tawhid even when facing a tyrant who claimed divinity. Later, by Allah’s leave, he migrated. With Hajar and Isma‘il he fulfilled the trial of settling a barren valley; with Isma‘il he raised the foundations of the Sacred House. He was tested with the command concerning his son and responded with submission. Ibn Kathir gathers these scenes so believers see a friend of Allah whose courage, intellect, and trust outweighed custom, kinship pressure, and fear of fire.

title.en: The Story of Isma‘il and Zamzam

content.en: Ibrahim brought Hajar and their nursing son Isma‘il to the barren valley of Makkah by Allah’s command, leaving them with a small water-skin and dates. When he turned to leave, Hajar asked if Allah had ordered this; hearing that He had, she said Allah would not neglect them. Ibrahim prayed that hearts would incline to them and that they would be given fruits so they might give thanks. The water finished. Hajar ran between Safa and Marwah seeking help until Zamzam sprang forth. Birds and travelers later settled near the water. Isma‘il grew among Jurhum; narrations describe Ibrahim’s visits, advice about Isma‘il’s household, and finally the raising of the Ka‘bah’s foundations with Isma‘il—father and son praying that their work be accepted and that a messenger arise from their offspring. content.en: Yaqub, also called Israel, was favored with prophethood. Tension with his brother led him to travel, seeking Allah’s protection with prayer and humility. Narrations in Ibn Kathir’s collection describe his journey, his household, and the twelve sons who became the tribes of Israel. He loved Yusuf deeply. When the brothers plotted and Yusuf was lost, Yaqub’s eyes whitened with grief, yet he never despaired of Allah’s relief, saying he complained of his sorrow only to Allah. Years later, the scent of Yusuf’s shirt restored his sight, and the family reunited in Egypt. Ibn Kathir recounts Yaqub as a father’s faith under long sorrow—patience that does not extinguish hope, and love that does not excuse injustice among brothers.

content.en: Lut settled near Sodom, a city known for highway robbery, public indecency, and hostility to strangers. He called them to fear Allah and leave their wrongdoing. They answered with threats to drive him out if he continued preaching. Even his wife inclined to the people’s side. Angels came as guests in handsome form. The people rushed toward Lot’s house. He pleaded with them and offered the protection of his household as a host, but they persisted. The angels revealed their mission, told Lut to leave by night with those who believed, and warned him not to look back. At dawn the town was overturned and ruined by a shower of stones—a severe lesson. Ibn Kathir also notes the angels’ visit to Ibrahim with glad tidings before they went to Lut’s people. The account teaches that mocking purity, harming guests, and rejecting a prophet after clear warning invite destruction, while those who obey are led out in safety.

content.en: Shu‘aib was sent to Madyan (and the people of the thicket): worship Allah alone, give full measure and weight, do not withhold from people what is theirs, and do not spread corruption or block the path of believers. Trade cheating had become normal; he tied marketplace honesty to faith itself. They ridiculed his prayer and clinging to fairness, and threatened the believers. After clear warning, a cry and torment seized the wrongdoers while Shu‘aib and those who believed were saved. Ibn Kathir presents this story so that justice in buying and selling is remembered as worship—and fraud as a path that destroyed a nation.

content.en: Yusuf’s brothers, jealous of their father’s love, cast him into a well. Travelers drew him out and sold him in Egypt. There he grew in beauty and trustworthiness. When tempted, he chose prison over disobedience, and in prison he interpreted dreams with knowledge from Allah. He interpreted the king’s dream of cattle and grain, advising storage for years of drought. Raised to authority, he managed the land with justice. His brothers came seeking food without recognizing him. Through measured tests—demanding they bring their youngest brother, then placing a cup in the baggage—he brought the family to repentance without public revenge. He revealed himself with mercy: “No blame upon you today; Allah forgives.” He settled his parents and brothers in honor. Ibn Kathir walks through the Quran’s long Yusuf narrative to teach that envy destroys, chastity elevates, patience in injustice is rewarded, and forgiveness can heal a household.

content.en: Ayyub was a grateful prophet blessed with family and wealth. Severe trial then struck his health, property, and children. He remained patient, remembering Allah without complaint that crossed into despair. People who had gathered around him in prosperity drifted away, yet he did not abandon worship. He called upon his Lord that harm had touched him and that Allah is the Most Merciful of the merciful. Allah answered, restored his health, and returned family and blessings as a mercy and reminder for the worshippers. Ibn Kathir holds Ayyub up as the emblem of sabr: affliction is not proof of Allah’s anger when the servant’s tongue and heart stay with Him.

content.en: Harun was Musa’s brother and supporter, gifted with eloquence to help carry the message to Pharaoh. Together they said: “We are messengers of the Lord of the worlds,” asking that the Israelites be sent with them and warning of punishment for denial. When Musa went to the appointed rendezvous with his Lord, Harun remained with the people. Some followed the Samiri into worship of the calf. Harun had advised and restrained them as far as he could; Musa later seized his beard in grief, then learned Harun had feared division. The Quran clears him as a sincere partner in prophethood. Ibn Kathir presents Harun as the ally whose speech and steadfastness completed Musa’s mission.

content.en: After Musa, Ibn Kathir mentions Hizqeel (often identified with Ezekiel) among those who called the Children of Israel when hearts grew hard. Reports speak of a people who fled death and were caused to die, then raised as a sign so they might know Allah’s power over life—reminding them that escape from decree is impossible and that revival belongs to Allah alone. Though details vary among narrations, the teaching Ibn Kathir preserves is clear: prophets after Musa continued to confront forgetfulness and fear, calling a covenant people back to the Lord who splits the grain and the date-stone and resurrects the dead.

timedCues.textAr: ذكر ابن كثير حزقيل فيمن بعث بعد موسى حين احتاج بنو إسرائيل لتجديد الرجاء والطاعة.

timedCues.textEn: Reports speak of a people who fled death and were caused to die, then raised as a sign so they might know Allah’s power over life—reminding them that escape from decree is impossible and that revival belongs to Allah alone.
timedCues.textAr: وترد أخبار عن هداية أحيت القلوب بعد الخوف والخسارة.

timedCues.textEn: Though details vary among narrations, the teaching Ibn Kathir preserves is clear: prophets after Musa continued to confront forgetfulness and fear, calling a covenant people back to the Lord who splits the grain and the date-stone and resurrects the dead.
timedCues.textAr: ومع تفاوت قوة التفاصيل يبقى الأصل: أن الله يرسل المذكرين كلما ضعف الناس.

content.en: Ilyas (Elyas/Elisha in some listings) was sent when Israelites inclined to an idol such as Ba‘l. He called them to abandon false gods and return to the worship of Allah alone. Many rejected him; Allah’s help came against the idolaters, and the call of tawhid was renewed. Ibn Kathir’s brief notice places Ilyas in the chain of reformers after Musa—proof that idolatry can return even among those who knew revelation, and that Allah raises callers who smash the prestige of false deities with clear reminder.

content.en: Shammil (Samuel) guided the Israelites when they asked for a king to fight in Allah’s way. He warned them about the duties of kingship, then—by Allah’s leave—Talut (Saul) was appointed. Ibn Kathir uses Shammil’s episode to teach that leadership is by Allah’s choice and that victory follows discipline, not mere numbers.

content.en: Dawud was a young man of courage and faith when he faced Jalut and killed him by Allah’s leave, turning fear into victory for the Israelites. Kingdom and prophethood were given to him. Mountains and birds glorified Allah with him; iron was made soft for his armor-making, a practical mercy for defense. He judged with justice, yet the Quran also recounts a trial concerning litigants that taught him haste in judgment must yield to fuller hearing. He turned to Allah in repentance and remained a devoted worshipper whose zabur (psalms) praised his Lord. Ibn Kathir presents Dawud as strength joined to remembrance: a warrior-prophet whose power did not cancel humility.

content.en: Sulaiman inherited Dawud’s prophethood and a kingdom unlike any other. Allah taught him the speech of birds, subjected the wind and the jinn to his command, and poured molten copper for his works. He reviewed the hoopoe, which brought news of Bilqis, the queen of Saba, and her people’s sun-worship. Sulaiman sent a letter calling her to Allah. Her throne was brought in an instant; she recognized the sign, abandoned sun-worship, and submitted with Sulaiman to the Lord of the worlds. He also prayed for a kingdom that should belong to none after him, and remained grateful in inspection of his horses and hosts. Ibn Kathir’s Sulaiman is mastery under tawhid—power used to invite, not to tyrannize.
content.ar: ورث سليمان النبوة لا المال عن داود. وعلّمه الله منطق الطير وسخّر له الجن والإنس والريح. ولما بعثت ملكة سبأ بالهدايا أبى موالاة الدنيا ودعاها إلى الإسلام لله. وسارت جنوده من إنس وجن وطير بأمر الله. ويقرن ابن كثير الملك بالشكر: فالسلطان أمانة لا لعبة.

content.en: Shi‘a (Isaiah) is recounted by Ibn Kathir among prophets who warned Israel and its kings when injustice and idolatry spread. He called rulers and people to return to Allah’s law, warning that neglecting revelation brings humiliation and that repentance restores dignity. His chapter, drawn from reports of earlier scriptures filtered through Muslim historians, serves Ibn Kathir’s aim: every age of the Children of Israel that forgot Musa’s covenant heard another voice until proof was completed against them.

content.en: Aramaya (Jeremiah) warned Jerusalem when corruption and alliance with wrong paths invited disaster. He called king and people to sincere repentance. When they persisted, the city faced ruin and exile—yet Allah’s promise of return and rebuilding remained for those who would turn back. Ibn Kathir narrates this as history of warning fulfilled: prophets do not invent doom; they announce the consequence already tied to injustice. The tears of Aramaya are the grief of a messenger who loved his people and could not force their hearts.
content.ar: أنذر أرميا قومه وقد فشا الظلم. ووصف ابن كثير الحصار والحكم القاسي بعد العصيان. فالإعراض عن نذر الأنبياء يذهب بالأمن والمقدّسات. والنبرة موقرة: تسقط المدن إذا سُخر من الحق. غير أن الإنذار نفسه رحمة لمن سمع.

content.en: Daniel was among the righteous of Israel in the time of exile under a mighty pagan king. He held to prayer and refused food and honors that compromised his faith. Enemies plotted until he was cast into a den of lions; Allah shut their mouths and brought him out safe, while falsehood was exposed. Ibn Kathir preserves the episode as tawakkul under empire: a believer may lack political power yet never lacks a Lord who vindicates those who refuse shirk and persist in salah.
content.ar: في الأسر أُلقي دانيال إلى أسود فلم تمسّه بإذن الله، وأُتي له بالرزق بأمر الله ولو في الجبّ. وحفظ ابن كثير ذلك آية على أن الله يحفظ من يشاء في السجون والقلوب. فالتوكل لا يموت في القيود. وتواسي المظلوم من غير إنكار لشدة الطغيان.

content.en: Uzair (Ezra) passed by a ruined town and wondered how Allah would bring it to life. Allah caused him to die for a hundred years, then raised him and showed food and drink unchanged while his donkey’s bones revived before his eyes. He said: “I know that Allah is able to do all things.” Some later exaggerated about him wrongly; Ibn Kathir recounts the Quran’s lesson without endorsing excess: resurrection is real, and reflection on ruined towns should lead to certainty in Allah’s power—not to ascribe divinity to a righteous servant.
content.ar: مرّ عزير على قرية خاوية فقال أنى يحييها الله بعد موتها. فأماته الله مائة عام ثم بعثه ليرى طعامه وحماره قد أُعيدا. فرجع إلى قومه آية على البعث وجدّد تعليم الكتاب. ويربط ابن كثير المشهد بآية البقرة. ولبّ القصة اليقين بالنشور بعد الموت.

content.en: Zakariyah served Allah in old age, guardian of Maryam in the mihrab. Seeing her provisions, he asked for a pure offspring. Angels gave glad tidings of Yahya, a name not given before. He asked for a sign and was told he would not speak to people for three nights except by gesture, while glorifying Allah morning and evening. Ibn Kathir ties Zakariyah’s answered prayer to hope for those who think the door of mercy is shut by age. Prophethood and righteous children are gifts Allah opens when servants call in secret and public with sincerity.
content.ar: كفل زكريا الشيخ مريم في المحراب ورأى عندها رزقاً من غير أوان. فدعا بذرية طيبة على الكبر والعقم. فبشّره الله بيحيى وجعل آيته ألا يكلم الناس ثلاث ليال سوياً. فخرج يومئ إليهم أن سبّحوا. ويرسم ابن كثير رقّة دعاء شيخٍ استُجيب له فوق العادة.

content.en: Yahya confirmed a Word from Allah, was noble and chaste, and a prophet from among the righteous. Even as a youth he was given wisdom: compassion, devotion, and courage to speak truth to rulers. He called people to repentance and purity of life. Ibn Kathir recounts that his integrity made him enemies among the corrupt; yet his short life shone as fulfillment of Zakariyah’s glad tidings—proof that Allah protects the message even when tyrants strike the messenger.

content.en: Isa son of Maryam was created by Allah’s command “Be,” without a father—his likeness in that is as Adam. Angels gave Maryam glad tidings of a pure boy. He spoke in the cradle in her defense, and later called the Children of Israel to worship Allah as his Lord and their Lord. He healed the blind and the leper by Allah’s leave, raised the dead by Allah’s leave, and told them what they stored in their houses—as signs, not as independent power. Disciples believed; enemies plotted. Allah raised Isa and protected him from those who claimed to have crucified him. Ibn Kathir insists on the Quranic creed: Isa is a servant and messenger, the Messiah, honored—but not a son of God, and not to be worshipped. His table-spread and miracles invite gratitude to Allah alone.
content.ar: خلق الله عيسى ابن مريم بكلمة منه من غير أب، رسولاً مؤيداً بالبينات. ونفى القرآن أن يكون لله ولد أو أنه ثالث ثلاثة. فدعا إلى عبادة الله وحده وصدّق ما بين يديه، ووقف ضد مادية جوفاء. فميلاده ومعجزاته آية لقدرة الله ورحمته لا شرك في الألوهية. ويختم ابن كثير ما قبل محمد ﷺ بتقرير أن عيسى عبد الله ورسوله.

timedCues.textEn: He spoke in the cradle in her defense, and later called the Children of Israel to worship Allah as his Lord and their Lord. He healed the blind and the leper by Allah’s leave, raised the dead by Allah’s leave, and told them what they stored in their houses—as signs, not as independent power.
timedCues.textAr: ونفى القرآن أن يكون لله ولد أو أنه ثالث ثلاثة.

timedCues.textEn: Disciples believed; enemies plotted. Allah raised Isa and protected him from those who claimed to have crucified him.
timedCues.textAr: فدعا إلى عبادة الله وحده وصدّق ما بين يديه، ووقف ضد مادية جوفاء.

timedCues.textEn: Ibn Kathir insists on the Quranic creed: Isa is a servant and messenger, the Messiah, honored—but not a son of God, and not to be worshipped. His table-spread and miracles invite gratitude to Allah alone.
timedCues.textAr: فميلاده ومعجزاته آية لقدرة الله ورحمته لا شرك في الألوهية.
